output.title: Rethinking weekly rhythms starts with one repeatable task
output.body:
If your weekly rhythm feels messy, don’t start with “AI everywhere.” Start with one repeatable task you already do by hand: inbox triage, invoice checks, or sales follow-up. For a small business, that is usually a better test than trying to automate the whole week in one go.

Use a simple filter. Is the task recurring? Does it have a clear input, a predictable rule, and a measurable output? If yes, it may be a good candidate for a bounded workflow decision. If not, keep it manual. Some work should stay stubbornly human; the spreadsheet is not offended.

The useful question is not “can AI do this?” It is “what part of this weekly job is repeatable enough to hand to a system, and what part still needs your judgment?” In Bareni’s work, that is the point of a diagnostic: identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and define the control around it.

A practical next step: audit one weekly task this week, write down its trigger, input, and output, and note the rule you use to decide the result. If the pattern is clear, you have a candidate for a small automation. If the pattern is fuzzy, you have your answer too.
